output.name: Telun

anatomy.part: the loose west end of the belt, the first knot tied
the second knot along the belt, on the upward bend
the large count-knot at the middle of the belt, the one untied first at the festival
the knot at the low dip of the belt
the knot at the sharp rise of the belt
the knot at the low dip beyond the rise
the far east end of the belt, where the cord is cut

output.myth: Aun tied the first knot in the Lamp Road's cord the day he wondered how many days a pair of hands could work before they gave out. So he tied one knot for every day of the year's labour and strung them on a belt across the road. Mother Hesk watched from the Spindle and said nothing, which was how she scolded. When he was done he cut the belt loose, as he cuts everything, and it went up into the sky and became Telun, the Knot Belt. Each festival one knot is untied so the count can be seen going down. The old women say Sil searches the road for the loose end every night, and Tavo, who cannot count, pulls at the belt to make the knots fly. When the last knot is loosed, the year is done, and we tie a new belt on our own wrists and begin.
output.verse:
Knot by knot we count
the long days of salt and hands
one loosed for the feast
